lines.text: OPS-2291 opened: remove 4 hosts from billing-meta (billing subsystem slow) operator=rkaur
draining 268 hosts, batch=all, min-capacity check: not configured
partition quorum lost for 6912 of 8192 partitions
no placement capacity available, rejecting PutObject
cold restart requires full metadata validation, ETA 2h+

question: Why did the metadata tier fall over?
options: Billing subsystem slowness backing up metadata requests
meta-index deploy crash-looping the index nodes
Mistyped capctl selector drained index and placement fleets
AZ power loss taking a large share of index hosts offline

explanation.cause: An ops glob meant for 4 billing hosts matched and drained 268 metadata hosts
explanation.why: capctl had no minimum-capacity floor and drained everything in one batch. The 'meta-*' glob matched meta-index and meta-placement as well as billing-meta, so index partitions lost quorum and placement had nowhere to put new objects. A cold restart of the index needs full validation, so recovery takes hours.
explanation.tell: The selector line: 268 hosts matched for a ticket about 4 billing hosts — and the host count fell off a cliff in a single step instead of degrading.

alert.title: report-exporter: nightly finance export failed (0 of 312 files)

lines.text: export run 2026-10-09 started, 312 files to upload
upload failed key=finance/2026-10-09/ledger-001.parquet: An error occurred (AccessDenied) when calling the PutObject operation: Access Denied
export run aborted: 0 of 312 files written
PutRolePolicy role=search-indexer policyName=s3-access by terraform-ci/run-8812 resource=arn:aws:s3:::search-snapshots/*

question: Tap the event that broke the export.

explanation.cause: Terraform rewrote the exporter’s inline policy to point at a different bucket
explanation.why: PutRolePolicy replaces the whole inline policy document. The new s3-access policy granted writes only on finance-reports-v2/*, so every PutObject to finance-reports was implicitly denied and came back AccessDenied — five minutes after the change, on the job’s first upload.
explanation.tell: It’s the only change to the report-exporter role, it landed minutes before the first AccessDenied, and its resource ARN names a bucket the exporter doesn’t write to.

lines.text: checkout-api v2026.10.09-3 rolled out to 48/48 tasks
botocore.exceptions.ClientError: An error occurred (ThrottlingException) when calling the GetParameter operation (reached max retries: 4): Rate exceeded

question: What’s causing the 500s?
options: KMS request quota exhausted decrypting SecureStrings
Per-request GetParameter calls exceeding SSM’s API rate
Task role lost ssm:GetParameter in the new task definition
Regional Systems Manager outage in us-east-1

explanation.cause: The release fetched SSM parameters on every request and blew the API rate limit
explanation.why: Parameter Store caps the request rate per account and Region. With ttl=0s every request across 48 tasks called GetParameter, so calls jumped from ~3/s to ~900/s. SSM answered with ThrottlingException, botocore burned its 4 retries with backoff, and checkout returned 500 after seconds of waiting.
explanation.tell: GetParameter calls/s jumped ~300× exactly at the deploy, the loader logs ttl=0s, and the error is ThrottlingException: Rate exceeded — not AccessDenied or a KMS error.

source.title: Resolve "ThrottlingException" or "Rate exceeded" errors in Parameter Store

question: Why won’t the group scale past 24?
options: Scaling capped by the Auto Scaling group’s max size
EC2 out of m6i.4xlarge capacity in those AZs
Launch template points at a deregistered AMI
On-Demand vCPU quota for the account is used up

explanation.cause: The account hit its Standard On-Demand vCPU quota, so EC2 refused new launches
explanation.why: On-Demand limits are counted in vCPUs per instance-family bucket across the whole Region, not per group. 24 render nodes × 16 vCPU plus batch-etl’s 8 × 16 is exactly 512, so every further launch was rejected and the group sat below desired capacity.
explanation.tell: The Status Reason names a vCPU limit of 512, and 24 × 16 + 128 = 512. A capacity shortage would say InsufficientInstanceCapacity, and max size is 80.

alert.title: webhook-dispatcher: 31% of deliveries failing to hooks.partner

lines.text: webhook-dispatcher v4.12.0 rolled out (http client: DisableKeepAlives=true)

items.value: 1 Elastic IP, shared by all private subnets

question: Why are partner deliveries timing out?
options: NAT gateway out of ports to that one destination IP:port
Partner rate-limiting us by silently dropping new SYNs
Node conntrack tables full, dropping new outbound flows
Egress security group change blocking outbound 443

explanation.cause: Disabling keep-alive exhausted the NAT gateway’s ~55,000 ports to one destination
explanation.why: Each NAT gateway IP supports up to 55,000 simultaneous connections per unique destination (IP, port, protocol). With keep-alives off, every webhook opened a new connection to 203.0.113.40:443. Once that space ran out, new connections failed and ErrorPortAllocation climbed, while other destinations kept working.
explanation.tell: Connections plateau just above 55k right after the keep-alive change, failures hit only the single-IP partner, and other HTTPS calls through the same NAT succeed.

alert.title: session-service: 503 rate 22%, 3 pods restarted in the last hour

lines.text: Exception in thread "http-nio-8080-exec-17" java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space
Heap dump file created [4192305114 bytes in 22.452 secs]
Liveness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503

items.value: v3.8.0, 2 days ago (adds per-user token cache)

question: What’s killing session-service?
options: Session traffic surge outgrowing the 4 GiB heap
Container memory limit OOM-killing the JVM pod
Unbounded cache filling the heap until it runs out
Long G1 GC pauses failing the liveness probe

explanation.cause: A cache with no eviction kept growing until the Java heap was exhausted
explanation.why: Each GC reclaimed less than the one before: the post-GC floor climbed from ~1.2 GiB to ~4 GiB over hours while traffic stayed flat. That’s retained objects — the new per-user token cache never evicts. Once the old generation filled, allocations failed and the JVM threw OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space.
explanation.tell: Sawtooth with a rising floor under flat traffic. The error is Java heap space with RSS well under the 6 GiB limit — the JVM ran out, not the container.

lines.text: [9318.945s][info][gc] GC(2202) Pause Young (Concurrent Start) (G1 Evacuation Pause) 3891M->3874M(4096M) 52.104ms
pricing-engine call timed out after 2000ms (412 in last 7s)

question: What’s behind the periodic 7-second spikes?
options: CFS CPU throttling from a tight container limit
Database lock waits stalling pricing queries
Heap leak about to throw OutOfMemoryError
Full GC stop-the-world pauses freezing the JVM

explanation.cause: Live set near -Xmx forced repeated multi-second full GCs that freeze the app
explanation.why: With ~3.4 GiB live in a 4 GiB heap, G1’s concurrent cycle couldn’t free space fast enough and fell back to Pause Full (G1 Compaction Pause), a stop-the-world collection. Every application thread froze for ~7s, so in-flight requests blew past caller timeouts.
explanation.tell: Each latency spike matches a Pause Full of ~6,900 ms, and the heap lands at ~3.4 GiB after every full GC — a flat floor, so it’s an undersized heap, not a leak.

alert.title: ledger-api: readiness failing on 9/12 pods, 504s at ingress

lines.text: http: Accept error: accept tcp [::]:8080: accept4: too many open files; retrying in 5ms
Readiness probe failed: Get "http://10.2.7.31:8080/healthz": context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream

question: Tap the line that reveals the root cause.

explanation.cause: Unclosed response bodies leaked sockets until the process hit its fd limit
explanation.why: Each fraud-scorer call left its response body unclosed, so the connection never went back to the pool and its socket stayed open. Sockets are file descriptors; at the 65,536 nofile limit accept4 returned EMFILE, the server stopped taking new connections, and probes and ingress requests timed out.
explanation.tell: accept4: too many open files is the cause; the timeouts are symptoms. Sockets to fraud-scorer climbed linearly for hours and flattened just under 65,536 — the nofile limit.

lines.text: HikariPool-1 - Thread starvation or clock leap detected (housekeeper delta=1m1s262ms114µs702ns).

renew sub_01HQ7T2K9W failed: java.time.DateTimeException: Invalid date 'February 29' as '2025' is not a leap year

question: Tap the line that explains the failed batch.

explanation.cause: Renewal code built Feb 29 of a non-leap year, and java.time rejected every date
explanation.why: The job computed the next renewal as LocalDate.of(year + 1, month, day). Every subscription due on 2024-02-29 asked for 2025-02-29, which doesn’t exist, so LocalDate threw DateTimeException for all 1,904. plusYears(1) would have clamped to Feb 28.
explanation.tell: The exception names the impossible date. The Hikari ‘clock leap’ warning is a red herring — chronyd shows the clock off by only 0.2 ms.

lines.text: post 38114872 edited by user 912833 (body 31288 chars), listed on homepage
slow request GET / 6912ms (top frame: RegexInterpreter.Go <- TextUtil.TrimUnicodeWhitespace)
Server www/web-07 is DOWN, reason: Layer7 timeout, check duration: 2001ms. 4 active and 0 backup servers left. 63 sessions active, 0 requeued, 0 remaining in queue

question: What took the whole site down?
options: Cache stampede after the homepage cache expired
Trim regex backtracking on one post pinning every CPU
Health check on / too strict, ejecting healthy hosts
Bot traffic exhausting web worker threads on /

explanation.cause: A whitespace-trim regex went quadratic on one post that every homepage view rendered
explanation.why: ^[\s\u200c]+|[\s\u200c]+$ retries \s+$ from every position in a long whitespace run that isn’t at the end of the string — ~200M checks for 20,000 spaces. The post sat in the homepage list, so each view and each health check (GET /) burned seconds of CPU until the LB marked every backend DOWN.
explanation.tell: CPU jumped right after one homepage post was edited, slow requests show RegexInterpreter.Go under a trim helper, and traffic and DB load were flat — work per request exploded, not volume.
